explanations.explanation: Nazareth it is, friend. Luke 1:26 says God sent Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth. Gabriel's flight plan had one stop, and it was a town, not a palace. I spent years in a junk drawer, so a town in Galilee sounds like a big upgrade to me.

Bethlehem is a good guess, since it comes up in the Jesus story later. But Luke 1:26 says God sent Gabriel to a town in Galilee called Nazareth. This is the place where Gabriel's visit happens, and the text says nothing about Bethlehem here. Keep that name in your back pocket, though.

Capernaum is in Galilee too, so you were in the right neighborhood, friend. But Luke 1:26 names the town as Nazareth. That's where God sent Gabriel. Close on the map, but not the address on this delivery.

Mary, yes. Luke 1:27 says the virgin's name was Mary, and she was pledged in marriage to Joseph. Remember that name, baker, because it's about to matter a whole lot. Gabriel didn't need to check the mailbox twice.
Hannah is a real name in the Bible, but she isn't in this passage. Luke 1:27 says the virgin's name was Mary. She's the one Gabriel is sent to, and she's pledged to Joseph.
Ruth is a great name, but she belongs to another story. Luke 1:27 says the virgin pledged to Joseph was named Mary. So the delivery goes to Mary's door, not Ruth's.

I'd love to say Mary took it with a calm sip of tea, but that's not what the text says. Luke 1:29 says Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be. So she was not perfectly calm. Honestly, I think I'd have been troubled too, and I'd have knocked over a whole tray of cookies.

False is right, friend. Luke 1:29 says Mary was greatly troubled at his words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be. An angel shows up with a big greeting, and she stops to think about it. Not calm at all, and I can respect that.
Son is right, baker. Luke 1:31 says, “you will conceive and give birth to a son…” That's the news Gabriel brings her. It's a lot to take in, and it's only verse 31.
Jesus is right, friend. Luke 1:31 says, “…you are to give Him the name Jesus.” Gabriel hands Mary the name before the baby is even born. That's a big thing to be told ahead of time.
Not a daughter, friend. Luke 1:31 says Mary will give birth to a son. Gabriel is clear about that. Easy one to swap, but the text says son.

John is a name from earlier in this story, since Elizabeth's son is John (Luke 1:13). But Luke 1:31 says Mary is to give her son the name Jesus. Two babies, two names, and I'd keep the labels straight.
Joseph is the man Mary is pledged to (Luke 1:27), so I see how the name stuck. But Luke 1:31 says the name Mary is to give her son is Jesus. Joseph is in the story, just not as the baby's name.

explanations.answer: The Son of the Most High
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Luke 1:32 says, “He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High…” Gabriel is not shy with the big titles. He's piling them on, and I'm taking notes with my mustache.
That sounds impressive, but it isn't what Gabriel says. Luke 1:32 says, “He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High…” That's the title in this passage. Hang on to that one.
A priest is a job people knew well, so I get the guess, friend. But Luke 1:32 says He will be called the Son of the Most High. That's the title Gabriel gives. Gabriel doesn't mention a priest here.
Nope, friend. Luke 1:33 says, “…and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!” Gabriel doesn't say it ends, he says it never does. No expiration date on this one.

False is right, baker. Luke 1:33 says, “…and He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!” Forever means forever. I've had a batch of cookies last about ten minutes, so forever is hard for me to picture.

explanations.answer: How can this be since I am a virgin
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. In Luke 1:34, Mary asks the angel, “How can this be… since I am a virgin?” It's a real question, asked plainly. And Gabriel answers it, which is the best part.

explanations.answer: Why would God pick someone like me
explanations.explanation: That's a question a lot of us would ask, friend, but it isn't what Mary asks. In Luke 1:34 she asks, “How can this be… since I am a virgin?” She asks how, and she doesn't say anything about being picked. The text gives us her words, so I'll stick with those.

explanations.answer: When exactly will the baby be born
explanations.explanation: That's a fair question to ask, but Mary doesn't ask it. In Luke 1:34 she asks, “How can this be… since I am a virgin?” She wants to know how it will happen. The text doesn't give her asking about a date.

The Holy Spirit, baker. Luke 1:35 says, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you…” Gabriel gives her a real answer to her real question. I love an angel who answers the question.

Gabriel is the one doing the talking, friend, but he isn't the one who comes upon her. Luke 1:35 says, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you…” Gabriel is the messenger here, and the Holy Spirit is who he points to.
Elijah was a prophet in Israel's history, so I see why he popped into your head. But he isn't in this passage. Luke 1:35 says, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you…” That's who Gabriel names.

Elizabeth is right, friend. Luke 1:36 says, “Look, even Elizabeth your relative has conceived a son in her old age, and she who was called barren is in her sixth month.” Gabriel gives Mary a real example she can point to. That's the same Elizabeth whose husband Zechariah heard the news earlier.
Anna is a name from the Bible, but she isn't who Gabriel mentions here. Luke 1:36 says it's Elizabeth, Mary's relative, who has conceived a son in her old age. She's the one called barren before.
Martha shows up in other Bible stories, but not in this one. Luke 1:36 says Gabriel points Mary to Elizabeth, her relative. She's the one who conceived a son in her old age.
True, baker. Luke 1:37 says, “For no word from God will ever fail.” Gabriel says it right after pointing to Elizabeth. That's a line worth writing on the inside of your apron.
It's actually true, friend. Luke 1:37 says, “For no word from God will ever fail.” Gabriel says it to Mary. I don't mind a trick question, but this one is a promise.

That's her answer, baker. Luke 1:38 says, “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” She heard the whole thing and said that. I think that's a lot of faith in one short sentence.

explanations.answer: Let me talk to Joseph first
explanations.explanation: Joseph is part of the story, but that's not what Mary says. Luke 1:38 says, “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” The text gives her answer to Gabriel, and it doesn't mention talking to Joseph first.

explanations.answer: Give me a sign to be sure
explanations.explanation: That's not what Mary says, friend. Luke 1:38 says, “I am the Lord’s servant,” Mary answered. “May it happen to me according to your word.” Gabriel did mention Elizabeth (Luke 1:36), but Mary doesn't ask for a sign.
